title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the key safety warnings to keep in mind when handling the inflator assembly and electronics module of the AAIR system during maintenance?
answer: This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What is the recommended procedure for testing the AAIR system circuits using the V23 diagnostic tool, and how are indications for each seat displayed?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

question: What are the necessary steps to ensure the V23 diagnostic tool is ready for use before connecting it to the airplane for AAIR system testing?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

question: What actions should be performed if the V23 system diagnostic tool shows an unsatisfactory indication during the AAIR system seat adjustment/test after the safety buckle has been connected and the cable interface assembly has been replaced?
answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

question: What are the recommended practices for cleaning the belt assembly and related components of the AAIR system to maintain functionality and prevent damage?
answer: AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. Buildup of dirt and unwanted material can cause problems with system operation, decrease the life of the system, and cause corrosion of the metal parts in the system. Clean the belt assembly, hoses, cables, inflation Use care to keep contamination and cleaning agents away from the Do not let any part of the AAIR soak in any solution. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. (1) Clean non-metallic parts with warm water and a household soap/laundry detergent and a moist (2) Flush the parts with clear water on a clean cloth. (3) Use a soft brush, and cold soapy solution to clean the webbing, air bag cover, and gas hose by hand. Use a household liquid soap or detergent (4) Let the belt assembly dry by air. question: What are the recommended procedures for securing the inflator assembly and verifying the correct positioning of the three-point air bag belt during restraint system installation?
answer: Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. question: What procedures should be followed if the LED lights do not display amber during the AAIR system diagnostic check?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What precautions should be taken if the V23 diagnostic tool is subjected to impact or damage before use?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

question: What actions should be performed if the V23 system diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory seat status after the safety buckle has been connected during the AAIR system adjustment/test?
answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the specific steps to troubleshoot the AAIR system if the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED lights do not display amber during the diagnostic check?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

question: What are the safety precautions and warnings associated with handling the inflator assembly and electronics module of the AAIR system during maintenance?
answer: This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What is the procedure for using the V23 diagnostic tool to test each seat in the AAIR system, and how are the LED indicators used to identify the status of each seat?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What procedures are recommended to verify the proper functioning of the restraint system after installation?
answer: Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. (1)  Remove and keep the shipping caps from the inflator-hose connector fitting. NOTE:  The shipping caps can be used again. (2) Put the inflator assembly into the mounting bracket. Do not tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket. (3) Remove and discard the end cap plug  from the three-point air bag belt hose. Do not remove the safety cable tie for the air bag connector tongue. NOTE:  If the three-point air bag belt is not new, and the inflator is new, apply a thin layer of Loctite 242 thread-locking compound on the hose barb threads before you attach the inflator assembly. (4)  Make sure that the three-point seat belt air bag belt is aligned correctly. NOTE:  If aligned correctly, the gas hose will be on top of the seat belt attachment hardware. NOTE:  The inflator hose connector fitting is a pressure fitting which must be fully extended onto the gas hose barb to make an airtight connection. (6) Attach the squib connector to the inflator assembly. (7) Tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket to between 21 and 25 inch-pounds of torque. (8) Attach the EMA to the floorboard with the washers, nuts, and bolts. (9) Connect the cable interface assembly to the EMVA. (a) Move the seat-back aft and forward to its maximum travel. (c)  Move the seat-base aft and forward to its maximum travel.  Do a functional test on the system. question: What procedures should be followed if the V23 system diagnostic tool continues to show an unsatisfactory indication after replacing the cable interface assembly and connecting the safety buckle during the AAIR system seat adjustment/test?
answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended storage practices for the AAIR system components to prevent damage and ensure proper function over time?
answer: Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware. Storage of SparesInflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the inflator assembly away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Electronics Module Assembly . NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the EMA is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the EMA to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the EMA assembly in a cool and dry area.  The EMA assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.

(5) Clean all spacers, washers, nuts, and bolts with a lint-free cloth and isopropyl alcohol. (6) Cover the cable opening into the EMVA with pieces of cloth. question: What procedures should be followed if the V23 system diagnostic tool displays an unsatisfactory indication before or after connecting the air bag safety buckle?
answer: CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. question: What is the proper sequence for connecting and testing each seat in the AAIR system using the V23 diagnostic tool?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

question: What are the recommended steps to troubleshoot the AAIR system if the V23 diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory condition after testing the safety buckle connection?
answer: CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended procedures for verifying the correct operation of the restraint system after completing the installation?
answer: Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. (1)  Remove and keep the shipping caps from the inflator-hose connector fitting. NOTE:  The shipping caps can be used again. (2) Put the inflator assembly into the mounting bracket. Do not tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket. (3) Remove and discard the end cap plug  from the three-point air bag belt hose. Do not remove the safety cable tie for the air bag connector tongue. NOTE:  If the three-point air bag belt is not new, and the inflator is new, apply a thin layer of Loctite 242 thread-locking compound on the hose barb threads before you attach the inflator assembly. (4)  Make sure that the three-point seat belt air bag belt is aligned correctly. NOTE:  If aligned correctly, the gas hose will be on top of the seat belt attachment hardware. The label will be on the aft side of the belt. (5) Connect the gas hose from the three-point air bag belt to the inflator assembly with the correct torque . NOTE:  The inflator hose connector fitting is a pressure fitting which must be fully extended onto the gas hose barb to make an airtight connection. (6) Attach the squib connector to the inflator assembly. (7) Tighten the clamps on the mounting bracket to between 21 and 25 inch-pounds of torque. (8) Attach the EMA to the floorboard with the washers, nuts, and bolts. (9) Connect the cable interface assembly to the EMVA.  Make sure that the cables and hoses of the AAIR are clear of the height-adjustment crank, the seat lock handle, and the seat-back adjustment lever.  Install the inertia reel  in the airplane. Refer to Chapter 25, Seat Belt! Restraints - Maintenance Practices.  Remove the safety cable tie from the air bag buckle tongue.  Do a seat operation test on the pilot's seat and copilot's seat. (a) Move the seat-back aft and forward to its maximum travel. (c)  Move the seat-base aft and forward to its maximum travel.  Do a functional test on the system.  Refer to the AMSAFE Aviation AAIR Supplemental Maintenance Manual, V23 System Diagnostic Tool - Operation and Maintenance Manual. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Adjustment/Test

question: What is the recommended maintenance procedure for ensuring the V23 diagnostic tool remains accurate when testing the AAIR system?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

question: What is the correct procedure for performing the AAIR system functional test on each seat using the V23 diagnostic tool, including steps for preparation, connection, testing, and disconnection?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

question: What are the specific steps involved in securing the inflator assembly and verifying the correct alignment of the three-point air bag belt during restraint system installation?
answer: Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. (8) Attach the EMA to the floorboard with the washers, nuts, and bolts. (9) Connect the cable interface assembly to the EMVA. (a) Move the seat-back aft and forward to its maximum travel. (c)  Move the seat-base aft and forward to its maximum travel.  Do a functional test on the system. question: What steps should be followed if the V23 system diagnostic tool shows an unsatisfactory indication during the AAIR system seat adjustment/test after the safety buckle has been connected?
answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the steps to troubleshoot the AAIR system if the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED lights do not show amber during the diagnostic check?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific steps should be taken if the V23 system diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory seat status before connecting the safety buckle during the AAIR system adjustment/test?
answer: The procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What precautions should be taken to ensure the V23 system diagnostic tool functions properly after it has been subjected to physical impact?
answer: CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What is the process for performing a system functional test of the AAIR circuits using the V23 diagnostic tool, and how are seat-specific indications displayed during the test?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific checks should be performed to verify the condition of the inflator assembly's hardware, hose connection, and electrical connection during an AAIR system inspection?
answer: Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the primary safety warnings to consider when handling the inflator assembly and electronics module of the AAIR system during maintenance?
answer: This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What steps should be taken if the V23 system diagnostic tool shows an amber, red, or no LED indication during the seat position test of the AAIR system?
answer: CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. question: What specific precautions should be taken when cleaning the AAIR system to prevent damage to its internal components and materials?
answer: AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. Buildup of dirt and unwanted material can cause problems with system operation, decrease the life of the system, and cause corrosion of the metal parts in the system. Clean the belt assembly, hoses, cables, inflation Use care to keep contamination and cleaning agents away from the Do not let any part of the AAIR soak in any solution. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. (1) Clean non-metallic parts with warm water and a household soap/laundry detergent and a moist (2) Flush the parts with clear water on a clean cloth. (5) Clean all spacers, washers, nuts, and bolts with a lint-free cloth and isopropyl alcohol. (6) Cover the cable opening into the EMVA with pieces of cloth. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What precautions should be taken when handling the V23 diagnostic tool to ensure accurate system testing?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the main safety warnings to observe when handling the inflator assembly and electronics module of the AAIR system during maintenance?
answer: This section gives maintenance information for the AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint . The AAIR is a self-contained, modular, three-point restraint system that protects occupants from head- impact injury during an accident. The AAIR system has four core components: the air bag assembly, the inflator assembly, the electronics module assembly , and the cable interface assembly. WARNING: Do not try to open the inflator assembly. Do not apply an electric current to the electronics connection. The inflator assembly is a stored, gas/energetic material device and can cause injury if accidentally deployed.

answer: Restraint System Installation . NOTE:  Keep the protective plastic bag on the air bag belt during installation to keep it clean. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What precautions should be taken before using the V23 diagnostic tool if it has been subjected to impact or damage?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

answer: AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the recommended procedures for troubleshooting the AAIR system when the V23 diagnostic tool indicates an unsatisfactory condition after testing the safety buckle connection?
answer: CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System TroubleshootingThe procedures in this section must be done if the V23 system diagnostic tool gives an unsatisfactory indication for the seats in the AAIR System Adjustment/Test. An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (2) If an unsatisfactory indication is given after the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the key considerations to prevent damage when cleaning the AAIR system's belt assembly, hoses, cables, and other components?
answer: AMVSAFE recommends that the AAIR components be cleaned on a regular  basis. Buildup of dirt and unwanted material can cause problems with system operation, decrease the life of the system, and cause corrosion of the metal parts in the system. Clean the belt assembly, hoses, cables, inflation Use care to keep contamination and cleaning agents away from the Do not let any part of the AAIR soak in any solution. This can cause damage to the AAIR system. Do not use too much water when you clean the AAIR parts. Too much water can cause damage to the internal components and cause them to be unserviceable. Only use sufficient cleaning agent to make minimal suds. Excess soap must be removed before the part is installed in the system. Do not dry the belt assembly in sunlight or near any source of heat. Do not dry clean the belt assembly. Do not put the belt assembly fully into Keep the isopropyl alcohol away from the webbing, air bag cover, and CAUTION: Do not use soap or water on metal parts. (1) Clean non-metallic parts with warm water and a household soap/laundry detergent and a moist (2) Flush the parts with clear water on a clean cloth. (3) Use a soft brush, and cold soapy solution to clean the webbing, air bag cover, and gas hose by hand. Use a household liquid soap or detergent (4) Let the belt assembly dry by air. (5) Clean all spacers, washers, nuts, and bolts with a lint-free cloth and isopropyl alcohol. (6) Cover the cable opening into the EMVA with pieces of cloth. Clean the inflator and cables by hand with a lint-free cloth and a cold water and mild soap solution.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What are the necessary safety precautions to observe when handling the V23 diagnostic tool prior to performing the AAIR system test?
answer: The AAIR diagnostic check gives a system functional test of the AAIR circuits. To find problems in system components, use a replace-and-test procedure. There are two seats to each AAIR system. The 1 LED light will show an indication for the first seat on the AAIR system circuit. The 2 LED light will show an indication for the second seat on the AAIR system circuit. Once the V23 system diagnostic tool  is connected to the airplane, a check of the system is done one seat at a time.The V23 system diagnostic tool uses a 9-volt battery that can be replaced. A check of the diagnostic tool must be done yearly. The label on the back of the diagnostic tool will show when a check of the tool needs to be done. The diagnostic tool must only be sent to AMVSAFE to be calibrated. CAUTION: Calibrate the V23 system diagnostic tool again before use if it is hit, shaken, or if it falls to the floor.Before the V23 system diagnostic tool is connected to the airplane, do the steps that follow. (1) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (2) Look at the Tool Battery Indicator LED light. (a) If the LED light is green, the battery condition is satisfactory. (b) If the LED light is red, replace the 9-volt battery on the back of the SDT.Do the System Functional Test. NOTE:  There are two seats in each AAIR system. This functional test must be completed for each AAIR system on the airplane. (1) Make sure that the seat belt safety buckles are not connected. (2) Remove the protective cap from the cable interface assembly. (3) Connect the V23 system diagnostic tool to the diagnostic connector. (4) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the ON position. (5) Look at the Seat Position PASS/FAIL LED light. (6) If the 1 and 2 LED lights are amber, do the steps that follow. If the 1 and 2 LED lights do not give an amber indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (a) Connect the air bag safety buckle on the first seat location. (b) If the 1 LED light is green, the AAIR system for that seat is satisfactory. (c)  If there is an amber LED light indication, a red indication, or no indication, troubleshoot the system. Refer to AMSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting. (d)  Disconnect the air bag safety buckle. (e)  Do steps (a) thru (d) again for the second seat location. NOTE:  For the second seat location, the 2 LED light will be used to give an indication. (7) Set the SDT ON/OFF Switch to the OFF position. (8) Disconnect the V23 system diagnostic tool from the diagnostic connector. (9) Put the protective cap on the cable interface assembly. AMVSAFE Aviation Inflatable Restraint  System Troubleshooting

An unsatisfactory indication by the seat LED light is an amber indication, red indication, or no indication. If the V23 system diagnostic tool gives a satisfactory indication after the replacement of the individual components, stop the troubleshooting procedure. (1) If an unsatisfactory indication is given before the safety buckle is connected, do the steps that follow. (a) Do a check of all connections and tighten loose connections that are found.  Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again if there are loose connections found. (b) Replace the cable interface assembly. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again. (b) Replace the air bag safety buckle. Do the Adjustment/Test procedure again.

title: INFLATABLE RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES AIRPLANES WITH AMSAFE INFLATABLE RESTRAINT SYSTEM
question: What specific aspects should be checked during an inspection of the AAIR system's air bag assembly?
answer: Do an inspection of the AAIR system parts. (1) Air bag assembly. (a)  Make sure that the attachments are tightly connected. (b)  Do a visual inspection for dirt, oil, grease, or other unwanted material. (c)  Do a check for wear on the edges of the belt. (d)  Do a check for damage of the stitching or fabric threads. (e).  Do a check for holes or wear on the air bag cover. (f)  Do a check of the end fittings, buckle, and connector for cracks, dents, or corrosion. (2) Inflator hose. (a) Do a check for frayed edges, wear, or tears. (3) Cable interface assembly. (a) Make sure that all attachments are tightly connected. (4) Inflator assembly. (a) Do a check for loose mounting hardware. (b) Do a check of the hose connection. (c)  Do a check of the electrical connection. (5) Electronics module assembly . (a) Do a check for loose connections and mounting hardware. Storage of SparesInflator Assembly. NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the inflator assembly is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the inflator assembly to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the inflator assembly in a cool and dry area. The inflator assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the inflator assembly away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the inflator assembly away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.Electronics Module Assembly . NOTE:  The maximum continuous storage time for the EMA is seven years from the date of manufacture. After seven years, send the EMA to AMSAFE Aviation for inspection and repair. (1) Keep the EMA assembly in a cool and dry area.  The EMA assembly must be kept at a temperature between -220F and 131 OF . (2) Keep the EMA away from sunlight, dust, moisture, and other contamination. (3) Keep the EMA away from high electromagnetic, radio frequency, and electrostatic environments. (4) Obey all local storage regulations.
